question.problem:
Suppose $a=[1,\,-1]^{T},$ and $b=[-2,\,1]^{T},$ and $p=3.$ Find the Minkowski distance between $a$ and $b.$

Rounded to three decimal places, ${d}_{p}(a,b)≈$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the Minkowski distance is defined as

$$
{d}_{p}(a,b)=‖a-b{‖}_{p}
$$

where for an $N$-dimensional vector $v,$

$$
‖v{‖}_{p}={({\sum }_{i=1}^{N}|{v}_{i}{|}^{p})}^{1/p}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}_{3}(a,b) & =‖a-b{‖}_{3} \\  & ={‖[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]‖}_{3} \\  & ={(|1-(-2){|}^{3}+|-1-1{|}^{3})}^{1/3} \\  & ={35}^{1/3} \\  & ≈3.271.\end{aligned}
$$
